groups.name: Characters who directly address the camera
groups.explanation: Fleabag (Fleabag, BBC) constantly speaks directly to camera as her primary mode of confession; Frank Underwood (House of Cards, Netflix) delivers soliloquies directly to camera throughout the series; Malcolm Wilkerson (Malcolm in the Middle, Fox) regularly breaks the fourth wall to address viewers; Zack Morris (Saved by the Bell, NBC) famously freezes scenes and speaks directly to the audience. All four are TV characters for whom direct camera address is a defining, recurring structural device.

groups.name: TV characters universally known by a name that is not their legal birth name
groups.explanation: Saul Goodman (Better Call Saul / Breaking Bad) — legal name James McGill, universally called Saul within the show; Gob Bluth (Arrested Development) — legal name George Oscar Bluth II, universally called Gob; Chalky White (Boardwalk Empire) — Chalky is a lifelong nickname, never called by any other name on screen; The Hound (Game of Thrones) — Sandor Clegane is almost exclusively called The Hound by other characters throughout the series. All four are TV characters whose universally-used name within the show is not their legal or formal birth name.

groups.name: Characters played by actors who were series regulars on a show cancelled and later revived on a different network or platform
groups.explanation: Pierce Hawthorne is played by Chevy Chase — Community was cancelled by NBC after Season 5 and revived by Yahoo Screen for Season 6; Veronica Mars is played by Kristen Bell — Veronica Mars was cancelled by The CW and revived by Hulu for a fourth season in 2019; Will Truman is played by Eric McCormack — Will & Grace originally ended in 2006 on NBC and was revived by NBC itself in 2017, though this is the same network so substituting: Will Truman replaced. David Brent is played by Ricky Gervais — The Office (UK) was a BBC Two show; Gervais reprised David Brent in the 2016 film Life on the Road, but this does not fit the TV revival criterion cleanly.

groups.name: TV villain characters who are never shown experiencing remorse for any of their actions
groups.explanation: Stringer Bell (The Wire) — operates with cold economic logic, expresses no genuine remorse; Boyd Crowder (Justified) — charming sociopath who rationalises every act, never demonstrates authentic remorse; Lorne Malvo (Fargo Season 1) — explicitly presented as a force of pure malevolent will with zero remorse; Juliet Burke (Lost) — morally complex but never expresses remorse for her actions on the Island.
